verdict.rationale: Amplitude's own Session Replay docs say users can go from a chart or funnel to the exact session, tie errors to UX, catch errors across sessions, and focus replays on specific users, so the core jump-to-replay flow is first-party. The docs do not explicitly describe opening replays filtered to the users who dropped off at a particular funnel step, nor jumping directly from a specific error event to the affected users' replays, and there is no hands-on corroboration. missing for 10: explicit documentation of funnel drop-off-step-to-replay filtering, explicit error-event-to-affected-user replay navigation, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a product-manager, I can jump from a funnel drop-off or an error event straight to session replays of the affected users

citations.quote: Go from a chart, funnel, or support ticket to the exact session.
Spot frustration, tie errors to UX, and measure engagement across every page.
Catch rage clicks, dead clicks, and errors across sessions.
Focus replays on specific users, pages, and flows.
Replay sessions with full event and network context.
